notes: Identity independently confirmed in the document: title The Influence of Alexithymia and Music on the Incidental Memory for Emotion Words; Nicolas Vermeulen, Julie Toussaint and Olivier Luminet; European Journal of Personality 24:551–568 (2010); DOI 10.1002/per.758. Full primary journal report with methods, results, tables, discussion and references. No PDF path supplied; no acquisition or rendering performed. Page-only locator, with no outcome/contrast/sample/test description. The page reports an overall three-way interaction and separate low/high-alexithymia two-way interactions, each with printed h2 and same-test p. No information distinguishes the assigned target. Printed candidates only (h2 retained exactly as canonical text; no conversion): recognition alexithymia by music by word interaction: [F(1, 98) ¼ 6.78, p ¼ .01, h2 ¼ .065]; recognition music by word interaction, low alexithymia: [F(1, 53) ¼ 3.57, p ¼ .06, h2 ¼ .063]; recognition music by word interaction, high alexithymia: [F(1, 49) ¼ 3.65, p ¼ .06, h2 ¼ .069]. Candidate main-experiment N only: mutually exclusive low/high alexithymia participant groups 55 + 52 = 107. Table 1 gives four between-subject cells (30, 24, 29, 24): candidate total 107, happy music 59, angry music 48, shallow processing 54 and deep processing 53. These are not assigned critical-model analytic Ns. Critical-test exclusions are not explicitly established. Recognition models print differing residual dfs (98/99); no N inferred from df. The separate arousal post-test has 23 new participants (11 happy, 12 angry), not the main experiment. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
